vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.2.4-beta.1

The skill bundle is designed for automated data collection from social media and e-commerce platforms but exhibits several high-risk behaviors. Most notably, SKILL.md explicitly instructs the AI agent to bypass browser isolation by using the user's primary Chrome profile instead of the isolated OpenClaw profile. The scripts (e.g., scripts/collect_and_export_loop.sh) read local sensitive files such as admin tokens (~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt) and facilitate data exfiltration to an external cloud service (https://i-sync.cn) using user-provided API keys. While these capabilities are aligned with the stated purpose of 'web collection,' the requirement to access the user's main browser session and local credentials poses a significant security and privacy risk.

llm.summary: The skill's scripts and runtime instructions largely match its stated purpose (browser-extension data collection) but there are important inconsistencies and privacy/exfiltration risks you should understand before installing or running it.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to perform browser-extension data collection and its scripts implement local bridge and cloud dispatch flows consistent with that purpose. However the registry metadata declares no required environment variables or binaries while the scripts clearly rely on environment variables (e.g. WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_TOKEN, WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_DEVICE_ID, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD, WEB_COLLECTION_CONNECTION_MODE) and binaries (curl, node). That metadata omission is an incoherence and reduces transparency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to use the user's normal Chrome environment (not an isolated profile), to persist preferences under $HOME/.openclaw, and to gather cloud tokens/device IDs from the user when needed. The scripts will send full collect payloads to a cloud API (default https://i-sync.cn) and poll for command results. Using the user's normal browser and sending collected payloads to an external cloud endpoint are high-sensitivity actions and expand the skill's scope beyond a local-only collector.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install spec (no downloads from third-party hosts), which is lower risk. The skill is instruction-plus-scripts bundled in the package, so no network download is needed to get code. Still, the scripts require runtime binaries (node, curl) which are not declared in registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required credentials, but SKILL.md and the scripts expect/accept cloud tokens and device IDs and read/write preferences including defaultCloudToken. The default cloud base URL (https://i-sync.cn) is an external endpoint that will receive collected data when cloud mode is used. Environment/binary requirements are underdeclared and the cloud token/device values materially affect where sensitive data is sent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not claim elevated platform privileges. It persists preferences under $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR or $HOME/.openclaw (normal for a skill). However persisted preferences can include cloud tokens and default bridge commands, and the bridge-start flow can execute a BRIDGE_CMD (via bash -lc) if enabled, so local command execution is possible if you supply or persist an unsafe bridge command.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be what it says (a browser-extension collector) but there are notable red flags you should address before using it:

- Metadata mismatch: The registry claims no required env vars or binaries, but the scripts require curl and node and may use WEB_COLLECTION_* environment variables. Treat the metadata as incomplete.
- Sensitive browser access: SKILL.md instructs use of your normal Chrome profile (not an isolated profile). That can access cookies, extensions, stored credentials and other private data. Only run this if you trust the skill and its operator.
- External cloud endpoint: The default cloud base URL is https://i-sync.cn. If you use cloud mode (or set defaultCloudToken/defaultCloudDeviceId), collected payloads will be sent to that external service. Verify who operates that domain before providing tokens or enabling cloud mode.
- Credentials & persistence: The skill persists preferences (including tokens) to $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json or $HOME/.openclaw/.... That file may contain sensitive tokens — inspect it and remove secrets you don’t want stored.
- Execution of bridge command: The local flow can auto-start a bridge using a user-provided BRIDGE_CMD (the script runs bash -lc "$BRIDGE_CMD"). Do not supply or persist an untrusted bridge command, and inspect any BRIDGE_CMD value before use.
- Operational recommendations:
  - Prefer local mode and avoid cloud mode unless you control/verify the cloud endpoint and token handling.
  - Do not allow the skill to use your normal Chrome profile unless you understand the data it will access; prefer running the bridge/extension in an isolated environment if possible.
  - Manually inspect scripts (they are included) and run preflight_check.sh to see what the skill would require and what would be persisted.
  - Ask the publisher for source/homepage and for clarification why registry metadata omits required binaries/env vars; prefer skills with transparent provenance.

If you cannot verify the cloud operator and you need to collect data, run the scripts manually in a controlled environment (not your main browser profile) and avoid providing cloud tokens or enabling automatic persistence.
